title: Uniform noise stability of polynomial threshold functions
statement: For every natural number $k$, the class of Boolean functions admitting a polynomial threshold representation of Fourier degree at most $k$ is uniformly noise stable: there is a function assigning a probability in $[0,1]$ to each noise parameter in $[0,1/2]$, tending to zero as the parameter tends to zero through positive values, that bounds the noise sensitivity of every function in the class at every such parameter.
